question: Who is credited with proposing the legal concept of the living will in 1967?
explanation: Luis Kutner proposed the legal instrument known as a living will in 1967 to allow individuals to document their treatment preferences in advance. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: What was the primary societal trigger for the emergence of the living will movement?

options.A: demands by insurance companies to reduce hospital stays
options.B: advances in medical technology that could artificially prolong the dying process
options.C: new federal taxes imposed on long-term terminal care
options.D: the sudden shortage of hospital beds in acute care facilities

explanation: The movement arose because modern technology made it possible to sustain vital signs long after meaningful recovery was impossible, raising new ethical dilemmas. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary function of a durable power of attorney for healthcare?

options.A: naming a surrogate to make medical decisions if the patient becomes incapacitated
options.B: authorizing the primary physician to override family objections
options.C: listing specific surgical procedures a patient forbids under any circumstance
options.D: designating how financial assets should be distributed after death

explanation: A healthcare proxy or durable power of attorney appoints a trusted individual to interpret wishes and make decisions when the patient can no longer speak. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: How does a living will fundamentally differ from a healthcare proxy?

options.A: a living will dictates specific treatment preferences, whereas a proxy designates a decision-maker
options.B: a living will is verbal, whereas a proxy must be notarized by a magistrate
options.C: a living will is created by physicians, whereas a proxy is written by lawyers
options.D: a living will only applies to financial matters, whereas a proxy handles clinical interventions

explanation: Living wills outline specific medical wishes for end-of-life care, while a proxy delegates the authority to make decisions to another person. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which ethical principle forms the primary foundation for advance directives?
explanation: Autonomy is the moral right of self-determination, empowering individuals to dictate their own healthcare choices. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h3)

question: How does the concept of informed consent apply to end-of-life care decisions?

options.A: it requires family consensus before any comfort measures can be initiated
options.B: it mandates that physicians choose the most aggressive treatment available
options.C: it includes the right to refuse life-sustaining interventions after understanding the prognosis
options.D: it prevents patients from changing their minds once a document is signed

explanation: Informed consent encompasses informed refusal, meaning competent individuals can decline treatments after weighing risks and benefits. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is a mandatory requirement for a living will to be considered legally valid?

options.A: it must be approved by the local medical ethics committee
options.B: the maker must be mentally competent at the time of drafting
options.C: the patient must be currently admitted to an intensive care unit
options.D: it must be written entirely by a licensed physician

explanation: Advance directives are only legally binding if the individual possessed decision-making capacity when the document was created. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why is proper documentation and chart placement of an advance directive critical in an acute care setting?

options.A: to prevent family members from visiting the patient outside visiting hours
options.B: to ensure rapid access by the clinical team during a sudden life-threatening crisis
options.C: to satisfy billing requirements set by national health insurance agencies
options.D: to reduce the hospital's overall tax liability for terminal patients

explanation: Quick retrieval of advance directives prevents unwanted resuscitation and ensures patient preferences guide emergent care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to the effective implementation of living wills?

options.A: universal agreement among family members regarding end-of-life care
options.B: vague phrasing and undefined medical terminology in the document
options.C: failure of patients to discuss their wishes with primary care providers
options.D: cultural and religious taboos surrounding discussions of death

explanation: Disagreement among family members is a major barrier; universal agreement would actually facilitate implementation rather than hinder it. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why does vague terminology like 'heroic measures' create clinical challenges for nurses and physicians?

options.A: it is subjective and lacks clear operational definitions for specific treatments
options.B: it requires court intervention before any comfort care can be given
options.C: it legally obligates the hospital to provide unlimited financial funding
options.D: it automatically invalidates the document under standard medical laws

explanation: Terms like heroic measures mean different things to different people, leaving care teams uncertain whether to use ventilators, dialysis, or vasopressors. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the primary reason nurses are well-positioned to discuss advance directives with patients?

options.A: they hold sole legal authority to draft binding healthcare proxies
options.B: they are legally required to witness every living will in the hospital
options.C: they have final decision-making power over patient discharge plans
options.D: they spend significant, continuous time at the bedside building rapport

explanation: Continuous bedside contact allows nurses to build trusting relationships, making them natural facilitators for discussing sensitive end-of-life topics. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: A nurse discovers that an alert patient has a living will requesting no mechanical ventilation, but the family is demanding full life support. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: immediately comply with the family to avoid emotional conflict on the ward
options.B: advocate for the competent patient's expressed wishes while facilitating a family conference
options.C: discharge the patient immediately so family members can care for them at home
options.D: remove the patient's chart from the unit to prevent the family from seeing it

explanation: A competent patient's current expressed wishes and advance directives take precedence, and the nurse must advocate for patient autonomy while supporting the family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)
